hero.h1: Directive 8020 Endings Guide | Outcomes and Turning Points
hero.intro: Understand confirmed story outcomes, related Steam achievements and how Explorer and Survivor handle replaying decisions in Directive 8020.

blocks.text: Directive 8020 uses a branching story: crew outcomes and decisions can change how a run finishes. This guide distinguishes outcomes described by official Steam achievements from instructions that would need a reproducible playthrough. It does not present an unverified count of endings or label an invented route as the canonical best ending. The examples below contain outcome spoilers.

sections.heading: Outcomes described by official Steam achievements

rows: A course for Earth is set with no intruders aboard.
A complete decision sequence or a guarantee that every crew member survives.
The crew can all be killed.
The only way to reach this outcome or the number of distinct ending scenes.
Young can send a distress signal to the Andromeda.
Every later consequence or how that outcome combines with other branches.

blocks.text: These are public PC achievement conditions, not an exhaustive ending catalogue. An achievement can describe a story event rather than a separate ending. Its name is retained in English so it can be checked against the linked Steam list; the condition is explained in this guide’s language. Check the corresponding platform list before applying it to console trophies.

sections.heading: Revisiting a decision with Turning Points

blocks.text: Explorer allows access to Turning Points during the story. Survivor keeps the first story’s consequences and unlocks Turning Points if you reach the ending. These are play styles, separate from difficulty options. Review the current in-game tree to choose a decision that is actually available in your save; the official feature description does not supply a universal checkpoint for each result.

items: Record the platform, installed version, play style and starting save.
Write down the exact choice shown in the game and which characters are present.
Change one decision, then record subsequent scenes and the final result instead of assuming an immediate dialogue change proves a new ending.
Keep story completion, a particular crew outcome and platform achievement completion as separate goals.

blocks.text: For an Earth-bound outcome, compare the conditions for Home Free with your actual final scenes. For a run focused on crew survival, record each character separately; a destination condition is not an all-survive guarantee. To investigate the Andromeda branch, distinguish the distress-signal event from any later consequence. The official descriptions establish these outcomes but do not justify guessing an exact button sequence.
